knowledge-base.overview: Vapor 4.x guardrails, patterns, and best practices for server-side Swift. Covers application setup with configure.swift, RouteCollection controllers, Fluent ORM models and migrations, DTOs with Validatable, custom AsyncMiddleware, JWT authentication, content negotiation, and XCTVapor integration testing. Applies to Swift 5.9+ Vapor projects building REST APIs, web apps, and backend services.

core-principles.principle: Use RouteCollection per resource. Every handler is annotated @Sendable. All types crossing the API boundary conform to Content.
Never expose Fluent models directly as API responses. Use request DTOs (Content + Validatable) and response DTOs (Content only). Always validate before processing.
Controllers handle HTTP only: parse request, call service, write response. Business logic, domain rules, and orchestration belong in Services/.
Never hardcode database credentials or JWT secrets. Read from environment variables in configure.swift. fatalError on missing required secrets.
All route handlers, middleware, and migrations use async throws. No callback-based PromiseKit patterns in new code.

guardrail.rule: Never expose Fluent models directly in API responses. Always map to a response DTO in the controller.
Always implement both prepare and revert in every AsyncMigration. Do not skip revert.
Never use autoMigrate in production. Call prepare explicitly: swift run App migrate.
guardrail.good: // configure.swift — development only if app.environment == .development { try await app.autoMigrate() }

guardrail.rule: Never hardcode database credentials or JWT secrets. Always read from environment variables. fatalError when required env vars are missing at startup.
Never use try! or fatalError inside request handlers. Throw Abort errors instead.
guardrail.bad: let user = try! await User.find(id, on: req.db)!

guardrail.rule: Annotate all route handler functions with @Sendable to satisfy Swift concurrency checking.
Validate request DTOs before processing: try CreateUserRequest.validate(content: req). Return 422 validation errors automatically via Validatable.
Implement all list endpoints with pagination. Never return unbounded query results.
guardrail.good: let result = try await User.query(on: req.db).paginate(PageRequest(page: page, per: per))

guardrail.rule: Mark all Fluent model classes as final and @unchecked Sendable. Provide an empty init() — Fluent requires it.
Configure JSON encoding globally in configure.swift (snake_case keys, ISO 8601 dates). Do not configure per-response.

notes.note: Controllers/ — HTTP routing only: parse, call service, respond
Services/ — business logic, orchestration, domain rules
DTOs/ — all request/response types; never Fluent models in responses
Migrations/ — schema changes with prepare and revert

quick-reference.item: final class, Model + Content + @unchecked Sendable, empty init() required
Request: Content + Validatable | Response: Content only | Never expose Model
throw Abort(.notFound, reason: "...") — never try! or force-unwrap
Always paginate list queries — never .all() on user-exposed endpoints
prepare + revert both required; enums before tables, reverse in revert
DATABASE_URL / DB_* / JWT_SECRET from env vars — never hardcoded
Development only — never in production config
Global encoder: snake_case + iso8601 in configure.swift
